subject: Post-call: capacity commitment checklist & integration plan
messages:
From: Amit Kapoor <amit.kapoor@mediaco.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Thanks — quick follow up from today's capacity discussion

Dylan / Marissa —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick write-up from our side while it's fresh. Key pain points we called out:
- Latency spikes during morning batch ingest (8–10am PST) causing timeouts in our search indexer.
- Security requirement: model inference must run inside an isolated VPC with no egress to public internet.
- Steady-state throughput is ~120 tokens/sec for our baseline gen workload, peaks up to ~700 tokens/sec during campaigns.

Goals we want to achieve with a dedicated deployment:
1) Guaranteed isolation for PHI-sensitive requests (VPC + disk encryption + KMS).
2) P95 token latency under 220ms for baseline traffic.
3) Predictable monthly spend and a path to add burst capacity during campaigns.

Questions for you:
- Rough reserved GPU sizing you believe would cover steady-state + 2x headroom for growth?
- Can Redwood provide a documented runbook for failover to hosted fallback if our private pool experiences degraded performance?
- What does the SLA look like for latency targets vs availability for a reserved pool?

I'll loop in procurement (cc'd: Priya) if you can send a short statement of work / quote we can take to legal.

Appreciate it —
Amit
Sr. Platform Engineer, MediCo Health

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Date: 2026-12-07T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick follow up from today's capacity discussion

Amit —

Great notes, appreciated. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps below.

Recap of pain & constraints:
- Isolation: private pool in your VPC with customer-managed subnets and optional egress controls. We support KMS and HSM integrations for key material.
- Latency target: P95 under 220ms for baseline is achievable; we'll size accordingly and run a short load validation.
- Throughput profile: steady ~120 t/s, peaks ~700 t/s — that maps to a reserved pool + burstable buffer.

Proposed high-level sizing (initial):
- Reserved: 4 x A100-class instances (quantized model build) for steady throughput and consistent latency.
- Burst: policy to allow additional on-demand instances up to +3 GPUs for short campaigns; can be configured as preemptible with graceful request routing.
- Isolation: dedicated tenant + VPC peering or private link, no public egress; audit logs retained for 90 days (extendable).

SLA notes:
- Availability: 99.9% for Dedicated pools with reserved capacity (monthly).
- Latency: we publish model-level latency profiles; contractable P95 latency SLOs for pinned model versions, with credits for missed SLOs (we'll draft exact language).

Deliverables I'll share by EOD tomorrow:
1) Short SOW / quote (PDF) with reserved vs burst pricing.
2) Integration checklist for networking and key management (spreadsheet).
3) Runbook excerpt for fallback to hosted API.

Ask from you: confirm procurement timeline and a target date for onboarding validation (you mentioned end of January).

Next steps / owners:
- Dylan: send SOW + price bands (tomorrow EOD).
- Marissa: will propose technical validation plan and test harness for load validation.
- Amit/Priya: confirm procurement lead and target onboarding week.

Thanks — looking forward to making this low-friction.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Thanks — quick follow up from today's capacity discussion

Amit — quick technical follow-up from our runtime/infra side.

Load validation and rollout plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (staging): deploy identical model build in isolated staging pool; run a 48-hour soak at 1.5x baseline to validate cache behavior and KV memory footprint.
- Phase 2 (canary): 10% traffic to dedicated pool for 2 business days, measure P95/P99 and tail behaviors.
- Phase 3 (ramp): step up to 50% then 100% over a week with autoscaling policies active.

Autoscaling suggestions:
- Continuous batching enabled for inference paths that tolerate ~50–80ms additional tail, default batching window 20ms.
- Scale-up trigger: sustained CPU/GPU memory pressure or p95 token latency > target for 3 consecutive mins.
- Burst policy: allow up to 3 on-demand GPUs for campaign windows with a 30-minute warmup to reduce cold-start tail.

Monitoring & observability requests from our side for the validation run:
- Token-level latency traces, token cost breakdown, model cache hit rate.
- Access to your telemetry workspace (read-only) or a shared dashboard link.

I attached a short procurement checklist we typically share with customers — helps speed legal/procurement review.

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
